facts.statement: Fusuisaurus remains were discovered in 2001 in the Xinlong Formation of Guangxi, China.
facts.quote: Fragmentary postcranial remains of this animal have been discovered in 2001 in the Xinlong Formation of Guangxi

facts.statement: The name Fusuisaurus means "Fusui lizard" and refers to the county where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: Fusuisaurus (meaning "Fusui lizard" from the name of the county where it was discovered)

facts.statement: The type species F. zhaoi was named to honor the Chinese paleontologist Zhao Xijin.
facts.quote: The type species is F. zhaoi, named in honour of Chinese paleontologist Zhao Xijin

facts.statement: Fusuisaurus is classified as a basal titanosauriform.
facts.quote: This sauropod has been described as a basal titanosauriform

facts.statement: The parent group of Fusuisaurus is Titanosauriformes.
Fusuisaurus belongs to the class Saurischia.
Fusuisaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
Fusuisaurus lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated that Fusuisaurus reached a length of 22 meters and a weight of 35 tons.
facts.quote: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul gave a length of 22 m and a weight of 35 t

facts.statement: Despite its large size, Fusuisaurus had a relatively low body mass.
facts.quote: Despite this, it is relatively light in body mass

facts.statement: Fusuisaurus had a humerus measuring 183.5 cm long.
facts.quote: This sauropod was a very large animal, as its humerus was 183.5 cm long
